**Role:** wiring and diagnostic technician

**System:** fused extra-low-voltage relay trainer

**Success:** switch the load and identify a fault from voltage evidence

## The problem

Use a five-terminal relay to control a protected lamp while keeping the coil
circuit and load circuit distinct. Identify terminals 30, 85, 86, 87, and 87a
from verified documentation.

## Initial schematic and prediction

Add a clean schematic showing source, fuse, switch, coil, suppression component,
contacts, load, and return. Mark the expected energized path and normally closed
path without crossing unrelated conductors.

## Test evidence

| Test point | Switch open | Switch closed | Example interpretation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Coil supply | 0.0 V | 11.9 V | control reaches coil |
| Terminal 30 to ground | 12.0 V | 12.0 V | fused load supply present |
| Terminal 87 to ground | 0.0 V | 11.8 V | contact changes state |
| Across lamp | 0.0 V | 11.7 V | load receives voltage |

## Fault and revision

With the poor-ground fault inserted, terminal 87 measured near source voltage but
the lamp remained off. Measuring across the ground connection exposed an
unexpected voltage drop. Repairing the return path restored operation.

## Conclusion

The relay separates control from the higher-current load path. A BeagleBone can
control an approved transistor or relay module, but its GPIO must never power an
automotive relay coil, lamp, or horn directly.
